spec_info.name: SDMMC Controller (3MCR) — SPC58 H-Line Reference Manual

nodes.name: SDMMC memory map
nodes.description: This page contains descriptive text about SDMMC clocks and interface control, but does not include the SDMMC memory map table.

nodes.name: Registers to generate SDMMC command
nodes.description: The requested table "Table 1809: Registers to generate SDMMC command" is not present on this page; the page shows Table 1808 (SDMMC memory map continued) which lists register offset addresses and their locations, not a bit-field register description table.

nodes.name: SDMASYSADDR field descriptions
nodes.description: This table describes the SDMA_SYSADDRESS field (bits 0:31) which serves dual purposes as the SDMA system address for DMA transfers and as Argument 2 for Auto CMD23 block count operations.

nodes.name: BLOCKSIZE field descriptions
nodes.description: This table describes the BLOCKSIZE register fields for the SDMMC controller, including SDMA buffer boundary settings (1:3) and transfer block size configuration (4:15) for DMA operations.

nodes.name: BLOCKCOUNT field descriptions
nodes.description: This table describes the BLOCKCOUNT field (bits 0:15, XFER_BLOCKCOUNT) which specifies the number of blocks to transfer in multiple block operations, with the hardware controller decrementing the count after each block until reaching zero.

nodes.name: ARGUMENT1 field descriptions
nodes.description: This table describes the ARGUMENT1 field for the SDMMC controller, specifying that bits 0:31 contain the MMC command argument corresponding to bits 39-8 of the command format.

nodes.name: TRANSFERMODE field descriptions
nodes.description: This table describes the TRANSFERMODE register fields for configuring block transfer mode (single/multiple) and data transfer direction (read/write) between host and card in the SDMMC controller.

nodes.name: Determination of transfer type
nodes.description: This table defines how the transfer type (Single, Infinite, Multiple, or Stop Multiple Transfer) is determined based on the Multi/Single block setting, Block count enable, and Block count values in the SDMMC controller.

nodes.name: COMMAND field descriptions
nodes.description: This table describes the COMMAND register fields including the command index (CMDINDEX) for specifying command numbers and the command type (CMDTYPE) for special commands like suspend, resume, and abort operations in the SDMMC controller.

nodes.name: RESPONSEn field descriptions
nodes.description: This table describes the COMMAND_RESPONSE field (bits 0:15) of the RESPONSEn register, which contains command response data transmitted on the SDMMC bus and is read-only with zero initialization at reset.

nodes.name: Determination of transfer type
nodes.description: This table defines the mapping between response type codes, index check enable, and CRC check enable parameters to determine the corresponding SDMMC response type name.

nodes.name: Response bit definition for each response type
nodes.description: This table defines the mapping between SDMMC response types and their corresponding response fields and register bit ranges.

nodes.name: DATAPORT field descriptions
nodes.description: This table describes the DATAPORT field, which provides a 32-bit data port register for accessing the host controller buffer.

nodes.name: PRESENTSTATE field descriptions
nodes.description: This table describes the PRESENTSTATE register fields for the SDMMC controller, detailing the signal level monitoring capabilities for DAT and CMD lines used for error recovery and debugging purposes.

nodes.name: HOSTCONTROL1 field descriptions
nodes.description: This table describes the PRESENTSTATE_INHIBITDAT and PRESENTSTATE_INHIBITCMD fields that indicate command inhibit status for DAT and CMD lines respectively in the SDMMC host controller.

nodes.name: POWERCONTROL field descriptions
nodes.description: This table describes the POWERCONTROL register fields for the SDMMC controller, including the SDBUS voltage selection bits (4:6) and the SD bus power control bit (7).

nodes.name: BLOCKGAPCONTROL field descriptions
nodes.description: This table describes the BLOCKGAPCONTROL register fields for controlling boot acknowledge checking and alternative boot mode access in eMMC card operations.

nodes.name: TIMEOUTCONTROL field descriptions
nodes.description: This table describes the TIMEOUT_CTRVALUE field in the TIMEOUTCONTROL register, which sets the data timeout period for the SDMMC controller based on card bus clock periods.

nodes.name: SOFTWARERESET field descriptions
nodes.description: This table describes the SOFTWARERESET field bits for the SDMMC controller, detailing software reset options for DAT line, CMD line, and full controller reset along with the registers and bits affected by each reset type.

nodes.name: NORMALINTRSTS field descriptions
nodes.description: This table describes the NORMALINTRSTS register fields for the SDMMC controller, including error interrupt status, boot complete/terminate interrupt, boot acknowledge receive status, and re-tuning event indicators.

nodes.name: Relation between transfer complete and data timeout error
Relation between command complete and command timeout error
ERRORINTRSTS field descriptions
nodes.description: This table describes the ERRORINTRSTS register field descriptions for the Secure Digital and MultiMediaCard controller (SDMMC), detailing various error interrupt status bits including host errors, DMA errors, auto command errors, data errors, timeout errors, and command index/end bit errors.

nodes.name: Relation between command CRC error and command timeout error
nodes.description: This table defines the four possible error states based on the combination of command CRC error and command timeout error bit values in an SDMMC controller.

nodes.name: NORMALINTRSTSENA field descriptions
nodes.description: This table describes the NORMALINTRSTSENA register fields for the SDMMC controller, defining interrupt status enable bits for various functions including boot operations, re-tuning events, INT_A/B/C signals, and card interrupt/removal detection.

nodes.name: ERRORINTRSTSENA field descriptions
nodes.description: The requested Table 1835 (ERRORINTRSTSENA field descriptions) is not present on this page; only the register bit diagram for ERRORINTRSTSENA is shown, with the field descriptions table likely appearing on a subsequent page.

nodes.name: NORMALINTRSIGENA field descriptions
nodes.description: This table describes the NORMALINTRSIGENA register field descriptions for the SDMMC controller, defining interrupt signal enable bits for various events including boot operations, re-tuning, and card interrupts.

nodes.name: ERRORINTRSIGENA field descriptions
nodes.description: The requested table "ERRORINTRSIGENA field descriptions" (Table 1837) is not present on this page; the page shows Table 1836 (NORMALINTRSIGENA field descriptions continued) and Figure 1853 (Error interrupt signal enable register), but the ERRORINTRSIGENA field descriptions table appears to be on a subsequent page.

nodes.name: AUTOCMDERRSTS field descriptions
nodes.description: This table describes the AUTOCMDERRSTS register fields for Auto CMD error status, including error types for CMD12, index errors, end bit errors, and CRC errors with their respective bit positions and descriptions.

nodes.name: Relation between auto CMD12 CRC error and auto CMD12 timeout error
nodes.description: This table defines the four possible error conditions based on the combination of Auto CMD12 CRC error and Auto CMD12 timeout error bit values, indicating no error, response timeout error, response CRC error, or CMD line conflict.

nodes.name: HOSTCONTROL2 field descriptions
nodes.description: This table describes the HOSTCONTROL2 register fields for the SDMMC controller, including preset value enable, asynchronous interrupt enable, sampling clock select, execute tuning, and driver strength select configurations.

nodes.name: CAPABILITIES31_0 field descriptions
nodes.description: The requested Table 1841 (CAPABILITIES31_0 field descriptions) is not present on this page; only the register diagram and the end of the previous table (1840) are visible.

nodes.name: CAPABILITIES63_32 field descriptions
nodes.description: This table describes the CAPABILITIES31_0 register fields for the SDMMC controller, including maximum block length, base clock frequency, and timeout clock configuration parameters.

nodes.name: MAXCURRENTCAP31_0 field descriptions
nodes.description: This table describes the MAXCURRENTCAP31_0 register field, specifically the CORECFG_MAXCURRENT3P3V field (bits 24:31) which defines the maximum current for 3.3V operation.

nodes.name: MAXCURRENTCAP63_32 field descriptions
nodes.description: This table describes the MAXCURRENTCAP63_32 register field descriptions, showing that bits 0:31 are reserved.

nodes.name: Maximum current value definition
nodes.description: This table defines the maximum current values for the SDMMC controller, mapping register values 0-255 to corresponding current levels ranging from 4 mA to 1020 mA, with register value 0 used to retrieve information via another method.

nodes.name: PRESETVALUEn field descriptions
nodes.description: This table describes the PRESETVALUEn register field, indicating that bits 0:15 are reserved with details provided in a separate table (Table 1847) for preset value register definitions.

nodes.name: Preset value register definition
nodes.description: Table 1847 defines the preset value registers for the SDMMC controller, listing register names, their memory offsets, descriptions of preset values for different speed modes (initialization, default, and high speed), and their associated signal voltage levels (3.3V).

nodes.name: SLOTINTRSTS field descriptions
nodes.description: This table describes the SLOTINTRSTS field (bits 15) which indicates the interrupt signal status for slot#0, combining interrupt and wakeup signals.

nodes.name: HOSTCONTROLLERVER field descriptions
nodes.description: This table describes the HOSTCONTROLLERVER register fields, showing vendor version number in bits 0:7 and specification version number in bits 8:15 for the Secure Digital and MultiMediaCard controller.

nodes.name: FORCEEVENTFORAUTOCMDERRSTS field descriptions
nodes.description: This table describes the FORCEEVENTFORAUTOCMDERRSTS register fields that control force event generation for various Auto CMD12 errors including command not issued, index errors, end bit errors, and CRC errors in the SDMMC controller.

nodes.name: FORCEEVENTFORERRINTSTS field descriptions
nodes.description: This table describes the FORCEEVENTFORERRINTSTS register fields used to force error interrupt events for ADMA errors, Auto CMD errors, current limit errors, and data end bit errors in the SDMMC controller.

nodes.name: ADMAERRSTS field descriptions
nodes.description: The requested Table 1852 containing ADMAERRSTS field descriptions is not present in this image; only the register diagram and introductory text are shown.

nodes.name: BOOTTIMEOUTCNT field descriptions
nodes.description: This table describes the BOOTTIMEOUTCNT field (bits 0:31) which contains the boot data timeout counter value used to determine DAT line timeout intervals during eMMC boot operations.

nodes.name: CORE_CONFIG field descriptions
nodes.description: This table describes the CORE_CONFIG register fields for the SDMMC controller, including settings for maximum current, slot type selection, asynchronous interrupt support, ADMA2 support, and base clock frequency configuration.

nodes.name: FB_CLK_SEL field descriptions
nodes.description: This table describes the FB_CLK_SEL field (bits 30:31) which selects the feedback clock source for loopback operations in the SDMMC controller, with options for internal delayed clock or external device pin connection.

nodes.name: DBG_STA1 field descriptions
nodes.description: This table describes the DBG_STA1 register field DMADEBUGBUS (bits 16:31), which provides DMA controller debug information including various host interface states, transfer modes, and state machine indicators for the SDMMC controller.

nodes.name: DBG_STA2 field descriptions
nodes.description: This table describes the DBG_STA2 register field CMDDEBUGBUS (bits 16:31), which contains CMD_CTRL debug bus signals for monitoring command FSM states and various SDMMC controller status indicators.

nodes.name: DBG_STA3 field descriptions
nodes.description: This table describes the DBG_STA3 register field TXDDEBUGBUS (bits 16:31), which contains various TXD_CTRL debug bus signals for monitoring SDMMC transmit and data transfer status.

nodes.name: DBG_STA4 field descriptions
nodes.description: This table describes the DBG_STA4 register field for the SDMMC controller, detailing the RXD_CTRL debug bus signals including receive status, stop conditions, and clock indications.

nodes.name: DBG_STA5 field descriptions
nodes.description: This table describes the DBG_STA5 register field RXDDEBUGBUS1, which provides debug bus signals for the RXD_CTRL module including end-of-block indications, clock control, and receive data state machine status.

nodes.name: Non-DMA transaction
nodes.description: The referenced Table 1862 for Non-DMA transaction is not displayed on this page; only a reference to it appears in section 57.4.1.

nodes.name: DMA transaction
nodes.description: This table describes the steps for non-DMA transaction sequence in the SDMMC controller, covering block reception, transfer completion handling, and abort procedures.

nodes.name: ADMA transaction flow
nodes.description: This table describes the step-by-step ADMA (Advanced DMA) transaction flow for read and write data transfers between the host controller and SD/MMC card, including interrupt handling and ping-pong FIFO buffer management.

nodes.name: Abort transaction
nodes.description: This table describes the step-by-step procedure for performing an ADMA (Advanced DMA) transaction flow on an SDMMC controller, covering register configuration, command issuance, interrupt handling, and error management.

nodes.name: Asynchronous abort
nodes.description: This table describes the three-step procedure for performing an asynchronous abort operation in the SDMMC controller, involving issuing an abort command, triggering software resets for DAT and CMD lines, and checking reset completion status.

nodes.name: 3MCR controller
nodes.description: This block diagram shows the 3MCR host controller architecture for SDMMC, consisting of master/target AHB interfaces, PIO/DMA controller, block buffer FIFO, control blocks (RECV_CTRL, CMD_CTRL, XMT_CTRL, CLK_GEN), and RX/TX flops connecting to the SDMMC interface.

nodes.name: Feedback clock selection
nodes.description: This block diagram shows the SDMMC feedback clock selection mechanism with two paths: Path A for direct clock output (up to 12MHz default speed) and Path B using a 4-input multiplexer for feedback clock selection supporting high speed modes up to 50MHz.

nodes.name: SDMA System address / Argument 2 register (SDMASYSADDR)
nodes.description: This figure shows the 32-bit SDMASYSADDR register layout at offset 0x0000, containing a single SDMA_SYSADDRESS field spanning all bits 0-31 with read/write access and a reset value of 0.

nodes.name: Block size register (BLOCKSIZE)
nodes.description: This figure shows the 16-bit BLOCKSIZE register layout at offset 0x0004, containing two fields: SDMA_BUFBOUNDARY (bits 3:0) for host SDMA buffer size configuration and XFER_BLOCKSIZE (bits 15:4) for transfer block size specification, with all bits reset to 0.

nodes.name: Block count register (BLOCKCOUNT)
nodes.description: This figure shows the 16-bit BLOCKCOUNT register layout at offset 0x0006, containing the XFER_BLOCKCOUNT field (bits 15:0) used for block count transfer operations in the SDMMC controller, with read/write access and a reset value of 0.

nodes.name: Argument 1 register (ARGUMENT1)
nodes.description: This figure shows the 32-bit ARGUMENT1 register layout at offset 0x0008, containing a single COMMAND_ARGUMENT1 field spanning bits 31:0 with read/write access and a reset value of zero.

nodes.name: Transfer mode register (TRANSFERMODE)
nodes.description: This figure shows the 16-bit TRANSFERMODE register layout at offset 0x000C with control fields for DMA enable, block count enable, auto command enable, data transfer direction, and multi-block select in bits 10-15, while bits 0-9 are reserved zeros.

nodes.name: Command register (COMMAND)
nodes.description: This figure shows the 16-bit COMMAND register layout at offset 0x000E for the SDMMC controller, with fields for command index, command type, data present, index/CRC check enable, and response type.

nodes.name: Response n register (RESPONSEn)
nodes.description: The RESPONSEn register is a 16-bit read-only register at offset 0x0010 + n*0x2 (where n=0 to 7) containing the COMMAND_RESPONSE field that stores command response data, with all bits reset to 0.

nodes.name: Data port register (DATAPORT)
nodes.description: The DATAPORT register is a 32-bit read/write register at offset 0x0020 containing the PIOBUFRDDATA field spanning all bits [31:0], with a reset value of 0x00000000.

nodes.name: Present state register (PRESENTSTATE)
nodes.description: This figure shows the 32-bit PRESENTSTATE register layout at offset 0x0024, which contains read-only status bits indicating the current state of SDMMC DAT lines, CMD line, card detection, write protection, and DMA transfer activity.

nodes.name: Host control 1 register (HOSTCONTROL1)
nodes.description: This figure shows the 8-bit Host control 1 register (HOSTCONTROL1) at offset 0x0028, containing fields for data width, high-speed enable, DMA select, extended data width, CD test level, and CD signal select configuration.

nodes.name: Power control register (POWERCONTROL)
nodes.description: This figure shows the 8-bit POWERCONTROL register at offset 0x0029 with read/write access, containing the PWRCTRL_SDBUSVOLTAGE field (bits 4:6) and SD_BUS_POWER field (bit 7), all reset to 0.

nodes.name: Block gap control register (BLOCKGAPCONTROL)
nodes.description: This figure shows the 8-bit BLOCKGAPCONTROL register layout at offset 0x002A with read/write access, containing fields for block gap control, boot acknowledgment, boot mode, interrupt, SPI mode, and wait control functions.

nodes.name: Wakeup control register (WAKEUPCONTROL)
nodes.description: This figure shows the 8-bit WAKEUPCONTROL register layout at offset 0x002B, with bits 5-7 controlling wakeup event enables for SD card removal, insertion, and interrupt respectively, while bits 0-4 are reserved as zero.

nodes.name: Clock control register (CLOCKCONTROL)
nodes.description: This figure shows the 16-bit CLOCKCONTROL register layout at offset 0x002C for the SDMMC controller, containing fields for internal clock enable, clock stability status, SD/MMC clock enable, and clock frequency selection bits.

nodes.name: Timeout control register (TIMEOUTCONTROL)
nodes.description: This figure shows the 8-bit TIMEOUTCONTROL register layout at offset 0x002E, with bits 7:4 containing the TIMEOUT_CTRVALUE field and bits 3:0 reserved as zeros, with read/write access and a reset value of 0x00.

nodes.name: Software reset register (SOFTWARERESET)
nodes.description: Register layout diagram showing the 8-bit SOFTWARERESET register at offset 0x002F with three writable software reset control bits (SWRESET_FOR_ALL, SWRESET_FOR_CMD, SWRESET_FOR_DAT) in bits 7-5 and reserved bits 4-0, all with reset value of 0.

nodes.name: Normal interrupt status register (NORMALINTRSTS)
nodes.description: This figure shows the 16-bit NORMALINTRSTS register layout at offset 0x0030, containing interrupt status flags for SD/MMC card operations including command complete, transfer complete, card insertion/removal, buffer ready, and boot-related status bits, most of which are write-1-to-clear (w1c).

nodes.name: Error interrupt status register (ERRORINTRSTS)
nodes.description: A 16-bit error interrupt status register (ERRORINTRSTS) at offset 0x0032 showing various error status bits for SDMMC controller including timeout, CRC, end bit, and index errors for both command and data operations, with write-1-to-clear (w1c) functionality.

nodes.name: Normal interrupt status enable register (NORMALINTRSTSENA)
nodes.description: A 16-bit read/write register at offset 0x0034 that enables normal interrupt status bits for the SDMMC controller, with individual enable bits for various interrupt sources including card insertion, card removal, and card interrupt status.

nodes.name: Error interrupt status enable register (ERRORINTRSTSENA)
nodes.description: Register layout diagram for the ERRORINTRSTSENA (Error interrupt status enable register) at offset 0x0036, showing 16 bits with various ERRORINTRSTS_ENABLEREGBITx fields for enabling error interrupt status, with Read/Write access and reset value of 0.

nodes.name: Normal interrupt signal enable register (NORMALINTRSIGENA)
nodes.description: This figure shows the 16-bit NORMALINTRSIGENA register layout at offset 0x0038, which controls normal interrupt signal enable bits for an SD/MMC controller, with all bits reset to 0.

nodes.name: Error interrupt signal enable register (ERRORINTRSIGENA)
nodes.description: A 16-bit read/write error interrupt signal enable register (ERRORINTRSIGENA) at offset 0x003A with enable bits for various error interrupt signals, where bit 4 and bits 0-2 are fixed at 0, and all other bits reset to 0.

nodes.name: Auto CMD error status enable register (AUTOCMDERRSTS)
nodes.description: This figure shows the 16-bit AUTOCMDERRSTS register layout at offset 0x003C, which contains error status enable bits for Auto CMD operations including NEXTERROR (bit 8), INDEXERROR (bit 11), ENDBITERROR (bit 12), CRCERROR (bit 13), TIMEOUTERROR (bit 14), and NOTEXECERROR (bit 15).

nodes.name: Host control 2 register (HOSTCONTROL2)
nodes.description: This figure shows the 16-bit HOSTCONTROL2 register layout at offset 0x003E for the SDMMC controller, containing fields for UHS mode selection, voltage signaling, driver strength, execute tuning, sampling clock selection, asynchronous interrupt enable, and preset value enable.

nodes.name: Capabilities[31:0] register (CAPABILITIES31_0)
nodes.description: This figure shows the 32-bit CAPABILITIES31_0 register layout at offset 0x0040, which is a read-only register containing HD implementation-specific capability fields including clock frequencies, voltage support, DMA support, and maximum block length settings.

nodes.name: Capabilities[63:32] register (CAPABILITIES63_32)
nodes.description: This figure shows the 32-bit CAPABILITIES63_32 register layout at offset 0x0044, containing read-only configuration fields for SPI block mode support, SPI mode support, re-tuning modes, and DDR mode support capabilities of the SDMMC controller.

nodes.name: Maximum current capabilities[31:0] register (MAXCURRENTCAP31_0)
nodes.description: A 32-bit read-only register layout showing the maximum current capabilities for 3.3V, with bits 31:24 containing CORECFG_MAXCURRENT3P3V field and bits 23:0 reserved, all reset to zero.

nodes.name: Maximum current capabilities[63:32] register (MAXCURRENTCAP63_32)
nodes.description: Register layout for MAXCURRENTCAP63_32 at offset 0x004C showing a 32-bit read-only register with all bits reserved and reset to 0.

nodes.name: Preset value n register (PRESETVALUEn)
nodes.description: A 16-bit read-only register layout for PRESETVALUEn showing bits 0-15, all initialized to 0 on reset, with offset calculated as 0x0060 + n*0x2 where n ranges from 0 to 7.

nodes.name: Slot interrupt status register (SLOTINTRSTS)
nodes.description: This figure shows the 16-bit SLOTINTRSTS (Slot interrupt status) register layout at offset 0x00FC, which is read-only with bit 15 containing the SDHCHOSTIF_SLOTINTRSTS field and bits 14-0 reserved as zeros with reset value of 0.

nodes.name: Host controller version register (HOSTCONTROLLERVER)
nodes.description: This figure shows the 16-bit read-only HOSTCONTROLLERVER register at offset 0x00FE, containing the SDHC vendor version number (bits 0-5) and specification version number (bits 6-15) fields with a reset value of 0x4008.

nodes.name: Force event for auto CMD error status register
nodes.description: This figure shows the 16-bit write-only FORCEEVENTFORAUTOCMDERRSTS register at offset 0x0050, which allows software to force various Auto CMD12 error status bits including NOTEXEC, TIMEOUTERR, CRCERR, ENDBITERR, INDEXERR, and CMDNOTISSUED errors.

nodes.name: Force event for error interrupt status register (FORCEEVENTFORERRINTSTS)
nodes.description: This figure shows the 16-bit FORCEEVENTFORERRINTSTS register layout at offset 0x0052, which is a write-only register used to force error interrupt events for testing purposes, with bits 15-6 controlling various error types (CMD timeout, CRC, end bit, index errors and data errors) and bits 5-0 reserved.

nodes.name: ADMA Error status register (ADMAERRSTS)
nodes.description: An 8-bit read-only ADMA Error status register (ADMAERRSTS) at offset 0x0054 showing bit fields for ADMAERRORSTATE (bit 7) and ADMALENMISMATCHERR (bit 5), with all bits reset to 0.

nodes.name: ADMA System address n register (ADMASYSADDRn)
nodes.description: A 16-bit read/write register layout showing the ADMA System address register (ADMASYSADDRn) with bits 15:0 containing the ADMA_SYSADDRESS field, all bits reset to 0, located at offset 0x0058 + n*0x2 where n ranges from 0 to 3.

nodes.name: Boot timeout control register (BOOTTIMEOUTCNT)
nodes.description: This figure shows the 32-bit BOOTTIMEOUTCNT register layout at offset 0x0070, containing a single field BOOT_TIMEOUTCNT spanning bits 0-31 for configuring the boot data timeout counter value, with a reset value of 0.

nodes.name: Core configuration register (CORE_CONFIG)
nodes.description: This figure shows the 32-bit CORE_CONFIG register layout at offset 0x0208, containing fields for SDMMC protocol clock frequency configuration (BASECLKFREQ_SDMMC_CLK), ADMA2 selection (CORECFG_ADMA2SUPPORT, CORECFG_ASYNCHINTRSUPPORT), slot type (CORECFG_SLOTTYPE), and maximum IO current value (MAXCURRENT_3P3V).

nodes.name: Feedback clock selection register (FB_CLK_SEL)
nodes.description: A 32-bit read/write register at offset 0x0210 used to program the feedback clock source, with the FEEDBACKCLK_SEL field occupying bits 30-31 and all other bits reserved as 0.

nodes.name: Debug status 1 register (DBG_STA1)
nodes.description: A 32-bit read-only debug status register (DBG_STA1) at offset 0x0220 containing the DMADEBUGBUS field spanning all 32 bits, providing a 16-bit wide DMA Control debug bus for software debugging, with all bits reset to 0.

nodes.name: Debug status 2 register (DBG_STA2)
nodes.description: A 32-bit read-only debug status register (DBG_STA2) at offset 0x0224 containing the CMDDEBUGBUS field in bits 31:16 and reserved zero bits in bits 15:0, used for CMD Control debug bus software debugging.

nodes.name: Debug status 3 register (DBG_STA3)
nodes.description: This figure shows the 32-bit read-only Debug status 3 register (DBG_STA3) at offset 0x0228, containing the TXDDEBUGBUS field in bits 23-24 for TXD module control debug bus software debugging, with all bits reset to 0.

nodes.name: Debug status 4 register (DBG_STA4)
nodes.description: A 32-bit read-only debug status register (DBG_STA4) at offset 0x022C showing the RXDDEBUGBUS0 field in bits 24-31 for RXD module control debug bus software debugging, with all other bits reserved and reset to zero.

nodes.name: Debug status 5 register (DBG_STA5)
nodes.description: A 32-bit read-only debug status register (DBG_STA5) at offset 0x0230, with RXDDEBUGBUS1 field in bits 31:24 and reserved zero bits in the remaining positions, used for RXD module control debug bus feedback during software debugging.

Features
57.1.1 
General description
The 3MCR (multi card reader) controller is an advanced host controller compliant with MMC 
specification version 4.51 and SD Host Controller standard specification version 3.0.
The 3MCR controller handles MMC/SD/SDIO protocols at transmission level, packing data, 
adding cyclic redundancy check (CRC), start/end bit, and checking for transaction format 
correctness.
The 3MCR controller provides programmed IO method and DMA data transfer method. In 
programmed IO method, the host processor transfers data using the Buffer data port 
register. Host controller supports both SDMA and ADMA2. ADMA2 is enabled by user using 
programming bit. DMA allows a peripheral to read or write memory without intervention from 
the CPU. The 3MCR host controller’s host controller System address register points to the 
first data address, and data is then accessed sequentially from that address.

nodes.description: The SDMMC controller supports MMC 4.51, SD Host Controller 3.00, SDIO 3.0, and SD Memory Card 3.01 specifications, offering data transfer rates up to 800 Mbits/s in DDR mode with 8-bit parallel data lines and host interface clock frequencies up to 100 MHz.

Up to 400 Mbits (50 Mbytes) per second data rate using 8 bit parallel data lines 
(mmc8 bit SDR mode) 
–
Up to 800 Mbits (100 Mbytes) per second data rate using 8 bit parallel data lines 
(mmc8 bit DDR mode)
–
Transfers the data in 1 bit, 4 bit and 8 bit modes and SPI mode

Cyclic redundancy check CRC7 for command and CRC16 for data integrity

Supports MMC plus and MMC mobile

SD/ SDIO card interface

Host clock rate variable between 0 and 50 MHz

Up to 200 Mbits (25 Mbytes) per second data rate in High speed mode

57.2.2 
Host controller core block description
The 3MCR host controller contains the major part of the design under 3MCR host controller 
core which contains the following blocks.
57.2.2.1 
Host interface (master/target)
The 3MCR host controller interfaces to the system bus using AHB master and AHB target 
interface.
The target bus is used to access the registers inside the host controller. Also when 
operating in PIO mode, the driver can access the Data port register through this interface. 
This is the PIO method in which the host driver transfers data using the Buffer data port 
register. The target bus supports only single transfer access (no burst support) and only one 
outstanding read/write transaction.
The master bus is used by the DMA controller (when using SDMA or ADMA2 modes). The 
DMA controller uses the master DMA interfaces to transfer data between the internal block 
buffer and the system memory and vice-versa. The DMA controller also uses the master 
interface to fetch the descriptors while operating in ADMA2 mode.
57.2.2.2 
Host controller register set
The host controller registers are dword accessible from the target interface. The host 
controller register set also implements the Data port register for the PIO mode transfers. 
The register set provides the control signals to rest of the blocks in design and monitors the 
status signals from the blocks to set interrupt status bits and eventually generate interrupt 
signal to the host bus.
The host controller register set acts as the bridge between host CPU and host controller.
The 3MCR controller registers are programmed by the host processor through host target 
interface. Interrupts are generated to the host processor based on the values set in the 
Interrupt status and Interrupt enable registers.

SDMMC IP does not provide error response for the accesses to reserved addresses. Also, it 
does not provide error response for the write accesses to read only registers or vice versa.
57.2.2.3 
PIO/DMA controller
The PIO/DMA controller module implements the SDMA and ADMA2 engines as defined in 
the host controller specification and maintains the block transfer counts for PIO operation. It 
interacts with the registers set and starts the DMA engine when a command with data 
transfer is involved. 
The DMA controller interfaces to the host master module to generate transfers and on the 
other side it interfaces with the block buffer to store/fetch block data. The DMA controller 
implements a separate DMA for SDMA operation and separate DMA for the ADMA2 
operation. In addition, it implements host transaction generator that generates controls for 
the host master interface module.
57.2.2.4 
Block buffer
The host controller uses a dual port block buffer (read/write on both ports) that is used to 
store the block data during data transfers. The size of the block buffer is 1 Kbyte, so that it 
can accommodate up to two 512B blocks. The block buffer uses circular buffer architecture. 
One side of the block buffer is interfaced with the DMA controller and operates on the host 
clock. The other side of the block buffer interfaces with control logic and operates on 
SDMMC card clock.
During a write transaction (data transferred from system processor to SDMMC card), the 
data is fetched from the system memory and is stored in the block buffer. When a block of 
data is available, the control logic will transfer it onto the SDMMC interface. The DMA 
controller continues to fetch additional block of data when the block buffer has space.
During a read transaction (data transferred from SDMMC card to system processor), the 
data from SDMMC card will be written in to block buffer and at the end when the CRC of the 
block is valid, the data is committed. When a block of data is available, then the DMA 
controller transfers this data to the system memory. The control logic meanwhile receives 
the next block of data provided there is space in the block buffer. If the host controller cannot 
accept any data from SDMMC card, then it will stop the data transfer from card by stopping 
the clock.
Note:
As the block buffer size is twice that of the block size, the block buffer behaves like a ping-
pong buffer.
57.2.2.5 
Clock generator
The clock generator module generates interface clock from the reference clock, based on 
the controls programmed in the Clock control register. These includes clock divider value 
and clock enable. The outputs from this module are the SDMMCCTRL_CLK and the 
SDMMCCARD_CLK. The SDMMCCTRL_CLK is used by the control logic and the 
SDMMCCARD_CLK connected to the output clock pin of SDMMC interface. This module 
also generates system resets to various clock domains.
57.2.2.6 
Timeout control
The timeout control logic implements the timeout check between block transfers. It uses the 
contents of the Timeout control register to implement timeout between blocks. This module 
operates under the control of the transmit control and receive control modules (based on

direction). When the timeout is detected the event is reported to transmit control or receive 
control module. 
57.2.2.7 
Command control
The command control module generates the command sequence on the CMD line of the 
SDMMC interface for every new command programmed by the software.
The command control module also implements the response reception and checking the 
validity of the response. It uses the response type field to determine the length of the 
response and the presence of CRC7 field. The response is received on the receive clock 
(which is the looped back clock). Once the response is received the contents of the 
response (start bit, command index, CRC7, end bit) are verified and response status is 
forwarded to the  register set module for setting various status bits. It also implements the 
timeout check on the response reception to make sure that the response is received with in 
the defined time (5 or 64 clocks based on command type). The received response is then 
stored into appropriate bit position in the Response register.
The command control module generates controls to the transmit control and receive control 
based on the transfer direction.
The command control module also generates auto command (AutoCMD12 or AutoCMD23) 
when enabled.
57.2.2.8 
Transmit control
The transmit control module is used for write transfers for transferring data to the card. Once 
the command is issued, this module waits for the block of data to be available in the block 
buffer and transfers this onto the DAT lines. Based on the configuration of data lines, the (1-
bit, 4-bit or 8-bits or SPI), the data from block buffer is appropriately routed. The CRC16 is 
individually calculated on per lane basis and is attached at the end of block transfer before 
the end bit. In case of DDR operation, it implements separate CRC16 for each edge of the 
clock.
At the end of block transfer, it waits for the CRC response on DAT0 line and reports the 
result of the CRC check to the register set.
Also this module checks for the write busy indication (DAT0 line) before transferring next 
block of data. The timeout check is implemented to make sure that the write busy is 
asserted no more than the required limit.
57.2.2.9 
Receive control
The receive control module is used for read transfers for receiving data from the card. Once 
the command is issued, this module waits for the block of data to be received from the card. 
Based on the configuration of data lines, the (1-bit, 4-bit or 8-bits or SPI), the data from 
SDMMC interface is assembled into byte and eventually into 32-bit word before it is being 
written into block buffer. The CRC16 is individually calculated on per lane basis and is 
checked against the received CRC16 at the end of block transfer before the end bit. In case 
of DDR operation, it implements separate CRC16 checker for each edge of the clock.
The data is received on the receive clock. This receive clock is the looped back clock 
(SDMMCCARD_CLK from the IO_BUF).
The timeout check is implemented to make sure that the gap between the block no more 
than the required limit.

57.2.2.10 Interface control
The interface control block maps the internal signals to the external SDMMC interface and 
vice versa. Based on the bus width (1/4/8) the internal signals are driven out appropriately.
The inputs from Rx flops module are latched on the rx_clk (looped back clock) and is output 
to the receive control module for further processing.
57.2.3 
Clocks
SDMMC_CLK: This is the main clock provided by CGM. It is used for the SDMMC interface 
side of the host controller. This clock input is used to generate sdmmcctrl_clk and 
sdmmccard_clk clocks based on the divisor value programmed by the host driver.
ahb_clk (commonly called as host_clk): host bus clock. The host bus interface modules, the 
register set and the DMA controller operate on this clock.
sdmmcctrl_clk: This clock is derived from SDMMC_CLK based on the Clock control register 
value programmed by the driver. This clock is used by the most of the control logic 
(command control, transmit control and sdmmc interface side of the block buffer).
sdmmccard_clk: same as sdmmcctrl_clk, except that this is available only when clock 
enable is set by the driver. This is the clock supplied to the card. 
The host controller supports both Full speed and High speed card. For High speed card, the 
host controller should clock out the data at rising edge of sdmmcctrl_clk and for Full speed 
card, the host controller should clock out the data at falling edge of sdmmcctrl_clk.
During read transaction when the read FIFOs are full, there is no space to accept one block 
of data from card, host controller will stop the clock to card so overrun condition will not 
occur at host controller side.
rxclk_in: This is the looped back clock either from the sdmmccard_clk or from the clk PAD of 
external memory device mounted on application board. This will account for the delay on the 
CLK being driven onto the SDMMC interface through the chip and the IO PAD. Refer to 
figure below for feedback clock selection.
Note:
To select the looped back clock software driver should program FEEDBACKCLK_SEL field 
of Feedback clock selection register (FB_CLK_SEL).

57.2.4 
Resets
The host controller uses asynchronous reset to reset the FF's, even though the reset itself is 
synchronous to the corresponding clock domain. ahb_reset_n is the primary reset input and 
is synchronized with corresponding clock domain. Internally an independent reset signal is 
generated for each of the clock domain from ahb_reset_n.
57.2.5 
Frequency range
The host_clk frequency is 100 MHz. For selection of clock frequency refer to Clocking 
chapter.
The sdmmcctrl_clk frequency range is 400 KHz to 50 MHz.
57.2.6 
FIFO overrun and underrun conditions in DMA and non-DMA 
transfers
57.2.6.1 
Write
During write transaction the host controller will transmit data to card only when a block of 
data is ready to transmit and also the card is not driving busy. So underrun condition will not 
occur on SDMMC host controller side.
In DMA mode host controller initiates DMA READ from host memory only if space is 
available to accept a block of data.
In non-DMA mode host controller will assert buffer write ready interrupt only if space is 
available to accept a block of data.

SDMA_SYSADDRESS

(1) SDMA system address 
This register contains the system memory address for a SDMA transfer. 
When the host controller stops a SDMA transfer, this register points to the 
system address of the next contiguous data position. It can be accessed 
only if no transaction is executing (after a transaction has stopped). Read 
operations during transfers may return an invalid value. The host driver 
initializes this register before starting a SDMA transaction. After SDMA has 
stopped, the next system address of the next contiguous data position can 
be read from this register. 
The SDMA transfer waits at the every boundary specified by the host 
SDMA buffer boundary in the Block size register. The host controller 
generates DMA Interrupt to request the host driver to update this register. 
The host driver sets the next system address of the next data position to 
this register. 
When the most upper byte of this register (0x003) is written, the host 
controller restarts the SDMA transfer. 
When restarting SDMA by the Resume command or by setting Continue 
request in the Block gap control register, the host controller starts at the 
next contiguous address stored here in the SDMA System address 
register. ADMA does not use this register. 
(2) Argument 2 
This register is used with the Auto CMD23 to set a 32-bit block count value 
to the argument of the CMD23 while executing Auto CMD23. 
If Auto CMD23 is used with ADMA, the full 32-bit block count value can be 
used. If Auto CMD23 is used without AMDA, the available block count 
value is limited by the Block count register. 65535 blocks is the maximum 
value in this case.

CMDTYPE
Command type 
There are three types of special commands: suspend, resume and abort. 
These bits are set to 00b for all other commands. 
Suspend command 
If the Suspend command succeeds, the HC assumes the eMMC Bus has 
been released and that it is possible to issue the next command which 
uses the DAT line. The HC de-asserts Read Wait for read transactions and 
stop checking busy for write transactions. The interrupt cycle starts, in 4-bit 
mode. If the Suspend command fails, the HC maintains its current state 
and the HD restarts the transfer by setting Continue request in the Block 
gap control register. 
Resume command 
The HD re-starts the data transfer by restoring the registers in the range of 
0x000–0x00D. The HC checks for busy before starting write transfers. 
Abort command 
If this command is set when executing a read transfer, the HC stops Reads 
to the buffer. If this command is set when executing a write transfer, the HC 
stops driving the DAT line. After issuing the Abort command, the HD issues 
a software reset.
00 Normal 
01 Suspend 
10 Resume 
11 Abort

Secure Digital and MultiMediaCard controller (SDMMC)
2929
22
DMACTRL_
RDXFERACTIVE
Read transfer active 
This status is used for detecting completion of a read transfer.
This bit is set to 1 for either of the following conditions:
– After the end bit of the read command.
– When writing a 1 to Continue request in the Block gap control register to 
restart a read transfer.
This bit is cleared to 0 for either of the following conditions:
– When the last data block as specified by block length is transferred to 
the system.
– When all valid data blocks have been transferred to the system and no 
current block transfers are being sent as a result of the Stop at block gap 
request set to 1. A Transfer Complete Interrupt is generated when this 
bit changes to 0.

This status indicates a write transfer is active. If this bit is 0, it means no 
valid write data exists in the HC. This bit is set in either of the following 
cases:
– After the end bit of the write command.
– When writing a 1 to Continue request in the Block gap control register to 
restart a write transfer. 
This bit is cleared in either of the following cases: 
– After getting the CRC status of the last data block as specified by the 
transfer count (single or multiple).
– After getting a CRC status of any block where data transmission is about 
to be stopped by a Stop at block gap request.
During a write transaction, a block gap event interrupt is generated when 
this bit is changed to 0, as a result of the Stop at block gap request being 
set. This status is useful for the HD in determining when to issue 
commands during write busy.

If this bit is 0, it indicates the CMD line is not in use and the HC can issue a 
command using the CMD line. This bit is set immediately after the 
Command register (0x00F) is written. This bit is cleared when the 
command response is received. Even if the Command inhibit (DAT) is set 
to 1, commands using only the CMD line can be issued if this bit is 0. 
Changing from 1 to 0 generates a Command Complete Interrupt in the 
Normal interrupt status register. If the HC cannot issue the command 
because of a command conflict error or because of command not issued

not set. Status issuing Auto CMD12 is not read from this bit. 
Auto CMD12 and Auto CMD23 consist of two responses. In this case, this

response of a read/write command. Status issuing Auto CMD12 is not read

SDMMCCLKFREQSEL
sdmmcctrl_clk frequency select (Lower bits)
This register is used to select the frequency of the sdmmccard_clk pin. 
The frequency is not programmed directly; rather this register holds the 
divisor of the base clock frequency for SDMMC_CLK clock in the 
Capabilities register. 
The length of divider is extended to 10 bits and all divider values are 
supported. 2 upper bits, [9:8], are programmable in 
clkctrl_sdmmclkfreqsel_upperbits field. 
0x3FF 1/2046 divided clock 
0xXXX 1/2N divided clock (Duty 50%) 
0x002 1/4 divided clock 
0x001 1/2 divided clock 
0x000 Base clock (10 MHz-254 MHz) 
The three default divider values can be calculated by the frequency that is 
defined by the Base Clock Frequency for SDMMC clock in the Capabilities 
register.
400 KHz divider value 
25 MHz divider value 
50 MHz divider value 
According to the Physical Layer specification, the maximum SDMMC 
clock frequency is 25 MHz in Normal speed mode and 50 MHz in High 
speed mode, and never exceeds this limit.
The frequency of SDCLK is set by the following formula: 
Clock Frequency = (Base Clock) / divisor 
Thus, choose the smallest possible divisor which results in a clock 
frequency that is less than or equal to the target frequency. 
For example, if the base clock frequency for SDMMC clock in the 
Capabilities register has the value 33 MHz, and the target frequency is 
25 MHz, then choosing the divisor value of 01h will yield 16.5 MHz, which 
is the nearest frequency less than or equal to the target. Similarly, to 
approach a clock value of 400 KHz, the divisor value of 40h yields the 
optimal clock value of 258 KHz.

This status is set if the HC detects the host DMA buffer boundary in the 
Block size register.
0 No DMA interrupt 
1 DMA interrupt is generated
13
NORMALINTRSTS_
BLKGAPEVENT
Block gap event 
If the Stop at block gap request in the Block gap control register is set, this 
bit is set.
Read transaction:
This bit is set at the falling edge of the DAT line active status (when the 
transaction is stopped at SDMMC bus timing. The Read Wait must be 
supported in order to use this function).
Write transaction:
This bit is set at the falling edge of write transfer active status (after getting 
CRC status at SDMMC bus timing).
0 No block gap event 
1 Transaction stopped at block gap

NORMALINTRSTS_
XFERCOMPLETE
Transfer complete 
This bit is set when a Read/Write transaction is completed.
Read transaction:
This bit is set at the falling edge of read transfer active status.
There are two cases in which the interrupt is generated. The first is when a 
data transfer is completed as specified by data length (after the last data 
has been read to the host system). The second is when data has stopped 
at the block gap and completed the data transfer by setting the Stop at 
block gap request in the Block gap control register (after valid data has 
been read to the host system).
Write transaction:
This bit is set at the falling edge of the DAT line active status.
There are two cases in which the interrupt is generated. The first is when 
the last data is written to the card as specified by data length and busy 
signal is released. The second is when data transfers are stopped at the 
block gap by setting Stop at block gap request in the Block gap control 
register and data transfers completed. (after valid data is written to the 
card and the busy signal is released).
Note: Transfer complete has higher priority than data timeout error. If both 
bits are set to 1, the data transfer can be considered complete.
0 No data transfer complete 
1 Data transfer complete
15

The timing of changing Auto CMD12 error status can be classified in three scenarios: 
1.
When the HC is going to issue Auto CMD12.
Set D00 to 1 if Auto CMD12 cannot be issued due to an error in the previous command.
Set D00 to 0 if Auto CMD12 is issued.
2. 
At the end bit of Auto CMD12 response.
Check received responses by checking the error bits D01, D02, D03, D04.
Set to 1 if error is detected.
Set to 0 if error is not detected.
3. 
Before reading the Auto CMD12 error status bit D07.
Set D07 to 1 if there is a command cannot be issued.
Set D07 to 0 if there is no command to issue. 
Timing of generating the Auto CMD12 error and writing to the Command register are 
asynchronous. Then D07 is sampled when driver never writing to the Command register. So 
just before reading the Auto CMD12 Error status register is good timing to set the D07 
status bit.

Occurs if the no response is returned within 64 sdmmcctrl_clk cycles from 
the end bit of the command.

meaningless.
0 No error 
1 Timeout

AUTOCMDERRSTS_
NOTEXECERROR

If memory multiple block data transfer is not started due to command error, 
this bit is not set because it is not necessary to issue Auto CMD12. Setting 
this bit to 1 means the HC cannot issue Auto CMD12 to stop memory 
multiple block transfer due to some error. If this bit is set to 1, other error 
status bits (D04 - D01) are meaningless. This bit is set to 0 when Auto 
CMD error is generated by Auto CMD23.

nodes.name: Non-DMA transaction (Chunk 2)
nodes.description: This section describes the non-DMA transaction sequence for the SDMMC controller, detailing the step-by-step process for configuring block transfers including register setup, command execution, interrupt handling, and the dual-FIFO buffer mechanism for write operations.

extras.full_text:

RM0452 Rev 4
         
Table 1862. Non-DMA transaction
Step
Description
1
Set the value corresponding to the executed data byte length of one block to Block size 
register.
2
Set the value corresponding to the executed data block count to Block count register.
3
Set the value corresponding to the issued command to Argument register.
4
Set the value to Multi / Single Block Select and Block Count Enable. Set the value 
corresponding to the issued command to Data transfer direction, Auto CMD12 Enable 
and DMA Enable.
5
Set the value to Multi / Single Block Select and Block Count Enable. Set the value 
corresponding to the issued command to Data transfer direction, Auto CMD12 Enable 
and DMA Enable.
6
Wait for the Command Complete Interrupt
7
Write 1 to the Command Complete in the Normal interrupt status register for clearing this 
bit.
8
Read Response register and get necessary information in accordance with the issued 
command.
9
In the case where this sequence is for write to a card, go to step (10-W).
In case of read from a card, go to step (10-R). 
10-W
Wait for Buffer Write Ready interrupt.
Non DMA Write transfer 
On receiving the Buffer Write Ready interrupt the system processor will act as a master 
and start  transferring the data via Buffer data port register (FIFO_1). Transmitter starts 
sending the data in SDMMC bus when a block of data is ready in FIFO_1. While 
transmitting the data in SDMMC bus the Buffer Write Ready interrupt is sent to the 
system processor for the second block of data. The system processor will act as a master 
and start sending the second block of data via Buffer data port register to FIFO_2. Buffer 
Write Ready interrupt will be asserted only when a FIFO is empty to receive a block of 
data. 
11-W
Write 1 to the Buffer Write Ready in the Normal interrupt status register for clearing this 
bit.
12-W
Write block data (in according to the number of bytes specified at the step (1)) to Buffer 
data port register.
13-W
Repeat until all blocks are sent and then go to step (14).
10-R
Non DMA Read transfer
Buffer Read Ready interrupt is asserted whenever a block of data is ready in one of the 
FIFOs. On receiving the Buffer Read Ready interrupt the system processor will act as a 
master and start reading the data via Buffer data port register (FIFO_1). Receiver start 
reading the data from SDMMC bus only when a FIFO is empty to receive a block of data. 
When both the FIFOs are full the host controller will stop the data coming from the card 
through Read Wait mechanism (if card supports Read Wait) or through clock stopping. 
Wait for Buffer Read Ready interrupt 
11-R
Write 1 to the Buffer Read Ready in the Normal interrupt status register for clearing this 
bit.
12-R
Read block data (in according to the number of bytes specified at the step (1)) from the 
Buffer data port register

DMA transaction
The burst types like 8-beat incrementing burst or 4-beat incrementing burst or single 
transfer is used to transfer or receive the data from the system memory mainly to avoid the 
hold of the Host/System bus by the master for a longer time.
The sequence for using DMA is shown in Figure 1876 and Table 1863.
Note:

should be disabled using EMMC_MSTR_EN_BYTE_SWAP (bit 27) of PCM REG3. This bit 
should be reset to 0. Reset value of this bit is 1. SDMMC driver should reset it.

nodes.name: DMA transaction (Chunk 2)
nodes.description: This section describes DMA read and write transfer operations for the SDMMC host controller, explaining the ping-pong FIFO mechanism used to increase throughput during data transfers between system memory and the SD/MMC card.

extras.full_text:
RM0452 Rev 4
2919/3897
RM0452
Secure Digital and MultiMediaCard controller (SDMMC)
2929
Note:
Step (2) and Step (3) can be executed at the same time. Step (5) and Step (6) can also be 
executed at the same time.
For example, if the host wants to transfer 4KB of data to the card. Assume the maximum 
block size is 512 bytes.
Then the host driver will program the Block size register as 512 and Block count register 
with the value 8.
The AHB master and transmitter residing inside the 3MCR host controller will get the 
information (how much data to transfer) from these registers. Using the above information, 
8
Write 1 to the Command Complete in the Normal interrupt status register for clearing this 
bit.
9
Read Response register and get necessary information in accordance with the issued 
command.
DMA read transfer 
On receiving the response end bit from the card for the write command (data flowing from 
host to card) the host controller will act as the master and request the System/Host bus. 
After receiving the grant the host controller will start reading a block of data from the system 
memory and fills the first FIFO. Whenever a block of data is ready the transmitter will start 
sending the data in SDMMC bus. While transmitting the data in SDMMC bus the host 
controller requests the bus to fill the second block in second FIFO. Ping-pong FIFOs are 
used to increase the throughput. Similarly the host controller reads a block of data from the 
system memory whenever a FIFO is empty. This will continue till all the blocks are read 
from the system memory. Transfer Complete Interrupt will be set only after transferring all 
the blocks of data to the card. 
DMA write transfer 
The block of data received from the card (data flowing from card to host) is stored in first 
half of the FIFO. Whenever a block of data is ready the host controller will act as the master 
and request the System/Host bus. After receiving the grant the host controller will start 
writing a block of data into the system memory from the first FIFO. 
While transmitting the data into system memory the host controller will receive the second 
block of data and store in second FIFO. Similarly the host controller write a block of data 
into the system memory whenever data is ready. This will continue till all the blocks are 
transferred to the system memory. Transfer Complete Interrupt will be set only after 
transferring all the blocks of data to the system memory. 
Note: Host controller will receive a block of data from the card only when it has room to 
store a block of data in FIFO. When both the FIFOs are full the host controller will 
stop the data coming from the card through Read Wait mechanism (if card supports 
Read Wait) or through clock stopping.
10
Wait for the Transfer Complete Interrupt and DMA Interrupt.
11
If Transfer Complete is set 1, go to Step(4) else if DMA Interrupt is set to 1, go to 
Step(12). Transfer Complete is higher priority than DMA Interrupt.
12
Write 1 to the DMA Interrupt in the Normal interrupt status register to clear this bit.
13
Set the next system address of the next data position to the System address register and 
go to Step (10).
14
Write 1 to the Transfer Complete and DMA Interrupt in the Normal interrupt status 
register to clear this bit.

nodes.name: Alternate boot operation (Chunk 0)
nodes.description: This section describes the eMMC4.3+ boot operation procedure for the SDMMC host controller, including boot acknowledgment handling, timeout management, boot data transfer, and termination sequences with associated interrupt servicing.

extras.full_text:
RM0452 Rev 4
2925/3897
RM0452
Secure Digital and MultiMediaCard controller (SDMMC)
2929
When the host driver sets the “boot_en” to 1 in Block gap control register and  
data_trans_direction bit to “1” in Transfer mode register, the host controller drives the cmd 
line to “0” for boot operation.
If the host controller is configured to wait for boot ack from the eMMC4.3+ device, the 
controller receives the boot acknowledgment and asserts the “boot_ack_rcv” interrupt to the 
driver.
If the host controller does not receive the boot acknowledgment from the device within the 
timeout value, the host controller will assert the data timeout error interrupt.
After servicing the boot acknowledge interrupt or data timeout error interrupt, the driver 
programs the Boot timeout control register with boot data timeout value.
The eMMC4.3+ device starts sending the boot data on the data line and host controller 
sends the same to system whenever a block of data is received from device.
The host controller terminates the boot operation when the programmed number of blocks is 
transferred to the system. The driver can write “boot_en” as “0” in Block gap control register 
and then driver waits for boot terminate interrupt. After the boot termination interrupt comes, 
the host driver issues soft reset for DATA line to the host controller to reset the data state 
machines to idle state.
The boot operation can also be terminated in between the boot transfer. Program the Stop 
at block gap request while transfer is going on and then wait for Transfer Complete Interrupt. 
Once the driver receives the Transfer Complete Interrupt the driver clears the boot enable 
and then the host driver issues soft reset for DATA line to the host controller to reset the data 
state machines to idle state.
There is no need to perform error recovery sequence in case data timeout interrupt occurs 
during boot operation (that is, ignore sending Abort command, soft reset and just clear the 
timeout interrupt and proceed with the boot flow).
If the device sends wrong acknowledgment to the host, the host controller will assert 
data_crc_err interrupt on the driver. In this case, the host driver has to stop the boot mode 
operation by setting boot_en as “0” in Block gap control register and write soft reset for cmd 
and data line.
If the device sends end bit as “0” in acknowledgment to the host, the host controller will 
assert data_end_bit_err interrupt on the driver.
The host driver stops the boot mode operation by setting boot_en as “0” in Block gap control 
register and write soft reset for cmd and data line.
Note:
Enable the boot_ack_chk bit during boot operation. If failed, the controller will not wait for 
boot acknowledge from the card and send out data CRC error when the card sends boot 
ack first and followed by boot data.
57.4.5.2 
Alternate boot operation
The host driver writes the boot timeout value as per the eMMC4.3+ spec into Boot timeout 
control register.
If the “alt_boot_en” and “boot_en” is set to 1 in Block gap control register and 
”data_trans_direction” bit is set to 1 in Transfer mode register, the host controller drives the 
CMD0 (0xFFFFFFFA) on the CMD line.
The system waits for Command Complete Interrupt before “boot_ack_rcv” interrupt.

extras.full_text:

If the host controller is configured to wait for boot ack from the eMMC4.3+ device, the 
controller receives the boot acknowledgment and asserts the “boot_ack_rcv” interrupt to the 
driver.
The eMMC4.3+ device starts sending the boot data on the data line and host controller 
sends the same to system whenever a block of data is received from device.
The host controller terminates the boot operation when the programmed number of blocks 
are transferred to the system and the driver programs “boot_en” and alt_boot_en as “0” in 
Block gap control register and then wait for boot terminate interrupt. Once the driver 
receives the boot termination interrupt. The driver needs to send CMD0 to inform the device 
about the boot operation complete. The driver programs Command register with argument 
“0x00000000” for the cmd0 (CMDTYPE as Abort) and waits for Command Complete. After 
that the driver need to issues the soft reset for data to host controller to reset the data state 
machines to idle state.
The boot operation can be terminated at any time. Program the Stop at block gap request 
while transfer is going on and then wait for Transfer Complete Interrupt. Once the driver 
receives the Transfer Complete Interrupt the driver clears the boot_en and alt_boot_en and 
then the host driver needs to send CMD0 to inform the device about the boot operation 
complete. The host driver programs Command register with argument “0x00000000” for the 
cmd0 (CMDTYPE as Abort) and waits for Command Complete. After that the driver need to 
issues the soft reset for data to host controller to reset the data state machines to idle state.
If the host controller does not receive the acknowledgment from the device with in timeout 
value the host controller will assert the data timeout error interrupt.
The driver programs the Boot timeout control register with boot data timeout value.
There is no need to perform error recovery sequence in case of data timeout interrupt as 
mentioned above.
If the device sends wrong acknowledgment to the host, then host controller will assert 
data_crc_err interrupt to the driver. The host driver has to stop the boot mode operation by 
setting alt_boot_en and boot_en as “0” in Block gap control register and write soft reset for 
cmd and data line.
If the device sends end bit as “0” in acknowledgment to the host, the host controller asserts 
data_end_bit_err interrupt on the driver. The host driver stops the boot mode operation by 
setting alt_boot_en and boot_en as “0” in Block gap control register and write soft reset for 
cmd and data line.
Note:
Enable the boot_ack_chk bit during boot operation. If failed, the controller will not wait for 
boot acknowledge from the card and send out data CRC error when the card sends boot 
ack first and followed by boot data.

can read the boot data as 2 Kbytes, 4 Kbytes, 1 Kbytes and 8 Kbytes instead of 128 Kbytes 
at a time).

nodes.name: SDMA System Address
nodes.description: Register at offset 0x000

fields.name: SDMA_SYSADDRESS
fields.raw: SDMA system address (Low) / Argument 2 (Low) (1) SDMA system address This register contains the system memory address for a SDMA transfer. When the host controller stops a SDMA transfer, this register points to the system address of the next contiguous data position. It can be accessed only if no transaction is executing (after a transaction has stopped). Read operations during transfers may return an invalid value. The host driver initializes this register before starting a SDMA transaction. After SDMA has stopped, the next system address of the next contiguous data position can be read from this register. The SDMA transfer waits at the every boundary specified by the host SDMA buffer boundary in the Block size register. The host controller generates DMA Interrupt to request the host driver to update this register. The host driver sets the next system address of the next data position to this register. When the most upper byte of this register (0x003) is written, the host controller restarts the SDMA transfer. When restarting SDMA by the Resume command or by setting Continue request in the Block gap control register, the host controller starts at the next contiguous address stored here in the SDMA System address register. ADMA does not use this register. (2) Argument 2 This register is used with the Auto CMD23 to set a 32-bit block count value to the argument of the CMD23 while executing Auto CMD23. If Auto CMD23 is used with ADMA, the full 32-bit block count value can be used. If Auto CMD23 is used without AMDA, the available block count value is limited by the Block count register. 65535 blocks is the maximum value in this case.
fields.abstract: System memory address register for SDMA transfers that holds the current/next contiguous data position and can also serve as Argument 2, initialized by the host driver before transfers and updated automatically as the transfer progresses.

nodes.name: Block Size
nodes.description: Register at offset 0x004

fields.name: SDMA_BUFBOUNDARY
fields.raw: Host SDMA buffer size. To perform long DMA transfer, System address register is updated at every system boundary during DMA transfer. These bits specify the size of contiguous buffer in the system memory. The DMA transfer waits at the every boundary specified by these fields and the HC generates the DMA Interrupt to request the HD to update the System address register. These bits support when the DMA support in the Capabilities register is set to 1 and this function is active when the DMA enable in the Transfer mode register is set to 1. 000 4 Kbytes (Detects A11 Carry out) 001 8 Kbytes (Detects A12 Carry out) 010 16 Kbytes (Detects A13 Carry out) 011 32 Kbytes (Detects A14 Carry out) 100 64 Kbytes (Detects A15 Carry out) 101 128 Kbytes (Detects A16 Carry out) 110 256 Kbytes (Detects A17 Carry out) 111 512 Kbytes (Detects A18 Carry out)
fields.abstract: Specifies the host SDMA buffer boundary size at which DMA transfers pause and generate an interrupt to request system address register updates for long DMA operations.

fields.name: XFER_BLOCKSIZE
fields.raw: Transfer block size. This register field specifies the block size for block data transfers for CMD17, CMD18, CMD24, CMD25, and CMD53. It can be accessed only if no transaction is executing (that is after a transaction has stopped). Read operations during transfer return an invalid value and Write operations are ignored. 0x0000 No data transfer 0x0001 1 Byte 0x0002 2 Bytes 0x0003 3 Bytes 0x0004 4 Bytes ... 0x01FF 511 Bytes 0x0200 512 Bytes
fields.abstract: Specifies the block size (0 to 512 bytes) for block data transfers used by CMD17, CMD18, CMD24, CMD25, and CMD53, and can only be modified when no transaction is in progress.

nodes.name: Block Count
nodes.description: Register at offset 0x006

fields.name: XFER_BLOCKCOUNT
fields.raw: Block count for current transfer. This register is enabled when Block count enable in the Transfer mode register is set to 1 and is valid only for multiple block transfers. The HC decrements the block count after each block transfer and stops when the count reaches zero. It can be accessed only if no transaction is executing (that is after a transaction has stopped). Read operations during transfer return an invalid value and Write operations are ignored. When saving transfer context as a result of Suspend command, the number of blocks yet to be transferred can be determined by reading this register. When restoring transfer context prior to issuing a Resume command, the HD restores the previously save block count. 0x0000 Stop count 0x0001 1 block 0x0002 2 blocks ... 0xFFFF 65535 blocks
fields.abstract: Specifies the number of blocks for multiple block transfers, decremented by the host controller after each block transfer until reaching zero, accessible only when no transaction is executing.

nodes.name: Argument 1
nodes.description: Register at offset 0x008

fields.name: COMMAND_ARGUMENT1
fields.raw: Command argument 1 The MMC command argument is specified as bit39-8 of Command-Format.
fields.abstract: Command argument 1 value corresponding to bits 39-8 of the MMC command format, used to specify parameters for MMC/SD card commands.

nodes.name: Transfer Mode
nodes.description: Register at offset 0x00C

fields.name: XFERMODE_MULTIBLKSEL
fields.raw:
Multi/Single block select
This bit enables multiple block data transfers.
0 Single block
1 Multiple block
fields.abstract: Enables selection between single block and multiple block data transfer modes.

fields.name: XFERMODE_DATAXFERDIR
fields.raw:
Data transfer direction select
This bit defines the direction of data transfers.
0 Write (host to card)
1 Read (card to host)
fields.abstract: Selects the data transfer direction, where 0 indicates a write operation from host to card and 1 indicates a read operation from card to host.

nodes.name: Command
nodes.description: Register at offset 0x00E

fields.name: COMMAND_CMDINDEX
fields.raw: Command index. This bit is set to the command number (CMD0–63, ACMD0–63).
fields.abstract: Specifies the command index number (0-63) for SD/MMC commands or application-specific commands to be sent to the card.

fields.name: COMMAND_CMDTYPE
fields.raw: Command type. There are three types of special commands: suspend, resume and abort. These bits are set to 00b for all other commands. Suspend command: If the Suspend command succeeds, the HC assumes the eMMC Bus has been released and that it is possible to issue the next command which uses the DAT line. The HC de-asserts Read Wait for read transactions and stop checking busy for write transactions. The interrupt cycle starts, in 4-bit mode. If the Suspend command fails, the HC maintains its current state and the HD restarts the transfer by setting Continue request in the Block gap control register. Resume command: The HD re-starts the data transfer by restoring the registers in the range of 0x000–0x00D. The HC checks for busy before starting write transfers. Abort command: If this command is set when executing a read transfer, the HC stops Reads to the buffer. If this command is set when executing a write transfer, the HC stops driving the DAT line. After issuing the Abort command, the HD issues a software reset. 00 Normal, 01 Suspend, 10 Resume, 11 Abort
fields.abstract: Specifies the command type, distinguishing between normal commands (00b) and special commands including suspend, resume, and abort operations that control data line transactions and bus release behavior.

nodes.name: Response n
nodes.description: Register at offset 0x010

fields.name: COMMAND_RESPONSE
fields.raw: Command response R[ ] refers to a bit range within the response data as transmitted on the SDMMC bus, REP[ ] refers to a bit range within the Response register. Note: These bits are read only bits and initialized to zero at reset.
fields.abstract: Contains bits [39:24] of the command response data received from the SDMMC bus, accessible as a read-only 16-bit field that is cleared to zero on reset.

nodes.name: Data Port
nodes.description: Register at offset 0x020

nodes.name: Present State
nodes.description: Register at offset 0x024

fields.name: SDMMC_DAT[7:4]
fields.raw: DAT[7:4] line signal level. This status is used to check DAT line level to recover from errors, and for debugging.
fields.abstract: Indicates the current signal level of SDMMC data lines DAT[7:4] for error recovery and debugging purposes.

fields.name: SDMMC_CMD
fields.raw: CMD line signal level. This status is used to check CMD line level to recover from errors, and for debugging.
fields.abstract: Indicates the current signal level of the CMD line, used for error recovery and debugging purposes.

fields.name: SDMMC_DAT[3:0]
fields.raw: DAT[3:0] line signal level. This status is used to check DAT line level to recover from errors, and for debugging. This is especially useful in detecting the busy signal level from DAT[0].
fields.abstract: DAT[3:0] line signal level status used for error recovery, debugging, and detecting the busy signal level from DAT[0].

nodes.name: Host Control 1
nodes.description: Register at offset 0x028

fields.name: PRESENTSTATE_INHIBITDAT
fields.raw: Command inhibit (DAT). This status bit is generated if either the DAT line active or the read transfer active is set to 1. If this bit is 0, it indicates the HC can issue the next command. Commands with busy signal belong to Command inhibit (DAT) (ex. R1b, R5b type). Changing from 1 to 0 generates a Transfer Complete Interrupt in the Normal interrupt status register. Note: The host driver can save registers in the range of 0x000-0x00D for a Suspend transaction after this bit has changed from 1 to 0. 1: Cannot issue command which uses the DAT line 0: Can issue command which uses the DAT line. Note: This bit is read only bit and initialized to zero at reset.
fields.abstract: Command inhibit status for DAT line indicating whether the host controller can issue the next command; set to 1 when DAT line is active or read transfer is active, and transitioning from 1 to 0 generates a Transfer Complete interrupt.

fields.name: PRESENTSTATE_INHIBITCMD
fields.raw: Command inhibit (CMD). If this bit is 0, it indicates the CMD line is not in use and the HC can issue a command using the CMD line. This bit is set immediately after the Command register (0x00F) is written. This bit is cleared when the command response is received. Even if the Command inhibit (DAT) is set to 1, commands using only the CMD line can be issued if this bit is 0. Changing from 1 to 0 generates a Command Complete Interrupt in the Normal interrupt status register. If the HC cannot issue the command because of a command conflict error or because of command not issued by Auto CMD12 error, this bit remains 1 and the Command Complete is not set. Status issuing Auto CMD12 is not read from this bit. Auto CMD12 and Auto CMD23 consist of two responses. In this case, this bit is not cleared by the response of CMD12 or CMD23 but cleared by the response of a read/write command. Status issuing Auto CMD12 is not read from this bit. So if a command is issued during Auto CMD12 operation, host controller manages to issue two commands: CMD12 and a command set by Command register. Note: This bit is read only bit and initialized to zero at reset.
fields.abstract: Indicates whether the CMD line is available for issuing a new command, being set when the Command register is written and cleared when a command response is received.

nodes.name: Power Control
nodes.description: Register at offset 0x029

fields.name: PWRCTRL_SDBUSVOLTAGE
fields.raw: eMMC bus voltage select. By setting these bits, the HD selects the voltage level. Before setting this register, the HD checks the voltage support bits in the Capabilities register. 111 3.3 Flattop. 110 Reserved. ... 000 Reserved. Note: only 3.3V is supported
fields.abstract: Selects the eMMC bus voltage level, with only 3.3V (value 111) supported; other values are reserved.

fields.name: SD_BUS_POWER
fields.raw: Before setting this bit, the SD host driver set SD Bus voltage select. If the HC detects the No card state, this bit is cleared. 1 Power on. 0 Power off
fields.abstract: Controls power to the SD bus, enabling (1) or disabling (0) power after the bus voltage has been configured, and is automatically cleared when no card is detected.

nodes.name: Block Gap Control
nodes.description: Register at offset 0x02A

fields.name: BLKGAPCTRL_BOOTACKENA
fields.raw:
To check for the boot acknowledge in boot operation.
1 Wait for boot ack from eMMC card
0 Will not wait for boot ack from eMMC card
fields.abstract: Controls whether the controller waits for a boot acknowledge signal from the eMMC card during boot operation.

fields.name: BLKGAPCTRL_ALTBOOTMODE
fields.raw:
To start boot code access in alternative mode.
1 To start alternate boot mode access
0 To stop alternate boot mode access
fields.abstract: Controls the start and stop of alternate boot mode access for boot code operations.
